statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 59 in the elevated band on an unresolved Saudi East-West pipeline outage, crude near 100 dollars, a completed Houthi takeover of the Bab el-Mandeb approaches and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence is 86 on a complete verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and the single shared reading applies to each instrument. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip of roughly 459 points that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, twenty hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: under the fixed repository mapping it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A shut tape deep into the weekend: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but mid-range, NQ retraced a 459-point round trip after firm core CPI, VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage, an Iraqi border closure and Monday's Oman meeting on Hormuz shipping all travel toward a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close. The cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished 105 points below the high, so the closing auction neither extended the advance nor broke it. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a four-day losing streak, though all three still finished the week lower and the Dow posted its worst week since March. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, closing near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range, and participation was broad rather than narrow: seven of eight tracked megacaps and five of seven large semiconductors closed higher, with Arm, Qualcomm and Intel leading while Nvidia and Micron finished marginally lower.

The macro backdrop is the source of the elevated Stress reading. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, with core at 0.3% against a 0.2% consensus and 2.4% on the year, and that upside core surprise lifted the market-implied probability of a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's FOMC to roughly 87%, from about 72% the prior day and near 50% a week earlier. The latest H.15 column carries the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95%. Crude eased on Friday, with WTI near $100.05 and Brent $104.61, but still finished the week 9.7% higher after Saudi Arabia shut its 7 million barrel per day East-West pipeline, the route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, following drone attacks launched from Iraqi territory. No restart timeline has been published. Overnight reporting added an Iraqi closure of the Shalamcheh crossing with Iran, the dismissal of the Maysan operations commander, a Saudi decision to withhold retaliation pending Iraqi measures, and a completed Houthi takeover of Mocha and the Bab el-Mandeb approaches. Iran's foreign ministry says Gulf states, Iraq and Iran will meet in Oman on Monday to discuss safe commercial shipping routes through Hormuz.

None of that can be traded inside this horizon. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, twenty hours after the last forecast slot ends. Every one of the twenty-four hours assessed here therefore describes a market with no venue, no quote and no mechanism by which accumulated headline risk can become the persistent no-retracement price path that the Tail score measures. Conditional Tail is held at a residual floor that steps from 5 to 8 across the window purely as a function of the growing stock of unpriced weekend information, and its maximum stays seventeen points below the 25-point block threshold. Stress traces a shallow valley and then firms, because decaying realized volatility is offset by a widening gap component. Confidence declines slowly from 86 to 78, which is a statement about distance from the last observed quote rather than about the quality of the evidence gathered.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 02:00 UTC on 11 September to 01:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at Tail 11 in mixed mode through the Asian session, then firms into a trend-up read between 06:00 and 11:00 UTC as European hours extended the advance, with Tail between 13 and 15. The 12:30 UTC inflation release marks the only departure from the low band: the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots were published at Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode, mapping to WATCH and a yellow status, with Confidence cut to 70 and 80 while the two-way reaction resolved. From 14:00 UTC the assessment returned to the low band in mixed mode near Tail 15 to 17, and the final five slots step down to 13, 7, 6, 5 and 5 in normal mode as the cash close passed and the futures halt removed the price path. Stress declined steadily across the window, from the mid-80s before the release to 59 in the closing slot, as realized volatility decayed and the event risk that had dominated the session was resolved rather than extended.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, twenty hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds that residual floor through the overnight and early Saturday European hours, then steps to 6 from 08:00 UTC, 7 from 14:00 UTC and 8 from 20:00 UTC as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows toward a reopen that still lies beyond the window. The maximum forecast value of 8 remains seventeen points below the 25-point block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and green in all twenty-four slots and no danger window is published. Stress traces a shallow valley, easing from 59 to 56 through the dead hours as Friday's realized volatility decays, then firming to 63 in the final slot on the unresolved pipeline outage, the completed Houthi takeover of the Bab el-Mandeb approaches, Monday's reported Oman meeting on Hormuz shipping and Wednesday's multi-stage policy sequence. Confidence decays from 86 to 78, a function of distance from the last observed quote rather than any weakening of the evidence gathered.
